blueprint line drawing.constraints: Draw it as an engineer's technical line drawing in isometric projection: crisp, even, unbroken strokes of one uniform medium weight, every edge and outline traced cleanly, with a few light construction lines carried a short way past the corners of the object itself. Ink every line in white or a pale ice blue only, and use the brand colors listed below for nothing except, at most, one very pale flat blue tint inside a few surfaces; leave every other surface unfilled. No shading, no hatching, no gradients, no glossy highlights, no dark or solid fills, and never black. Keep it to a few large, clearly separated parts with clean silhouettes rather than many small fiddly pieces. Leave the background fully empty and transparent behind, around and beneath the subject: no backdrop, no floor, no ground shadow, no frame, no border, no soft glow and no vignette, so the whole drawing lifts off the page in one piece.

prompts.subject: a classic wind-up kitchen timer: a squat round body on a short round base, a large dial face with evenly spaced tick marks around its rim and a single pointer hand, and a chunky twist knob on top, seen in three-quarter view
a gear train of three large interlocking spur gears of different sizes, each one thick disc with broad square teeth, a round hub and four spokes, meshed together side by side on parallel axles

a long straight conveyor belt unit: one wide belt looped over a large roller at each end, carried on a sturdy frame with four legs, with two plain closed cartons resting on the belt one behind the other

a neat stack of five cafeteria trays, each a shallow rounded rectangular tray with a raised rim, stacked squarely on top of one another, with the top tray lifted a little above the stack as if it is being taken off

the Dataslope marmot mascot, a friendly round alpine marmot with a cream belly, rosy cheeks, and small rounded ears, working as a draftsperson: standing beside a tilted drafting table, holding a pencil up in one paw and a large set square in the other
